appearance: A humanoid of immense size, with skin like weathered stone and hair like palm fronds.
behavior: Slow-moving and generally peaceful, but can cause earthquakes when he shifts his weight.
habitat: The deep ocean floor, ancient mountains
cultural_significance: A geological myth explaining the unique topography of the archipelago.
summary: Island-shaping giant from Palau
fun_fact: The Rock Islands are said to be the footprints of Uab.
seo_description: Uab (Chuab): the colossal giant who shaped the islands of Palau.
source: Palauan oral tradition

name: Delal a Ngibtal
description: A divine serpent that guards the purity of the reefs and the health of the ocean.
appearance: A long, elegant serpent with scales that reflect every color of the rainbow.
behavior: Guides lost fish and helps divers find the richest fishing grounds if they show respect.
cultural_significance: A symbol of the sacred bond between the Palauan people and the sea.
summary: Reef guardian serpent from Palau
fun_fact: The serpent is said to sing a song that can calm the most violent waves.
seo_description: Delal a Ngibtal: the divine reef serpent of Palauan mythology.
source: Palauan oral tradition

name: Ngirngemelas
description: A forest spirit known for its ability to confuse senses and lead travelers in circles.
appearance: A small, agile humanoid with skin that mimics the colors of the jungle leaves.
behavior: Loves to steal small items and rearrange the forest paths to baffle intruders.
cultural_significance: A reminder of the unpredictability and mystery of the natural world.
summary: Trickster forest spirit from Palau
fun_fact: It is said that if you walk backward for ten steps, you can break the Ngirngemelas's spell.
seo_description: The Ngirngemelas: the mischievous forest spirits of Palauan mythology.
source: Palauan oral tradition

name: Ossobó
description: A mystical bird whose song can influence the weather and bring rain to the forests.
appearance: A bird with iridescent blue feathers and a long, flowing tail.
behavior: Sings at dawn to awaken the earth; its song is said to be the voice of the ancestors.
cultural_significance: A symbol of hope, renewal, and the connection to ancestral spirits.
summary: Rain-bringing bird from São Tomé and Príncipe
fun_fact: The Ossobó is said to only sing when the heart of the listener is pure.
seo_title: Ossobó – São Tomé and Príncipe Folklore
seo_description: The Ossobó: the mystical rain-bird of São Toméan mythology.
source: São Toméan oral tradition

name: Te Pusi mo te Ali
description: A mystical fish, half-eel and half-flounder, that governs the health of the lagoon.
appearance: A long, shimmering fish with wide fins and skin that changes color with the water.
behavior: Ensures the abundance of fish; can cause the lagoon to turn murky if the waters are polluted.
cultural_significance: A symbol of the fragile balance of the island ecosystem.
summary: Lagoon guardian fish from Tuvalu
fun_fact: Legend says that Te Pusi mo te Ali can speak to humans through the ripples in the water.
seo_title: Te Pusi mo te Ali – Tuvalu Folklore
seo_description: Te Pusi mo te Ali: the guardian fish of Tuvaluan mythology.
source: Tuvaluan oral tradition

name: Tefolaha
description: A legendary spirit-hero who used his immense strength to lift the islands out of the sea.
appearance: A giant humanoid with skin like basalt and hair like sea-grass.
behavior: Protects the islands from erosion; creates new landmasses by piling coral and sand.
cultural_significance: Represents the resilience and creation of the Tuvaluan homeland.
summary: Island-building hero from Tuvalu
fun_fact: Tefolaha is said to sleep beneath the largest island, holding it steady against the waves.
seo_description: Tefolaha: the legendary island-builder of Tuvaluan mythology.
source: Tuvaluan oral tradition

name: Telematua
description: A colossal giant from the dawn of time, whose footsteps created the deep channels between the islands.
appearance: A humanoid of staggering proportions, with a voice that sounds like crashing waves.
behavior: Generally indifferent to humans, but can be awakened by great noise or disaster.
cultural_significance: A geological myth explaining the formation of the archipelago's channels.
summary: Ancient giant from Tuvalu
fun_fact: The deepest parts of the lagoon are said to be where Telematua rests his head.
seo_description: Telematua: the ancient giant of Tuvaluan mythology.
source: Tuvaluan oral tradition

name: Tepuhi
description: A divine serpent that governs the ebb and flow of the tides around the islands.
appearance: A long, shimmering serpent with scales that transition from turquoise to deep indigo.
behavior: Regulates the water levels; can cause tidal bores if the ocean is polluted or disrespected.
cultural_significance: A symbol of the rhythms of the sea and the dependency of the islands on the tide.
summary: Tide-controlling serpent from Tuvalu
fun_fact: Tepuhi is said to communicate with the moon to synchronize the tides.
seo_description: Tepuhi: the divine tide-serpent of Tuvaluan mythology.
source: Tuvaluan oral tradition
